title: MYOPATHY, MYOFIBRILLAR, 9, WITH EARLY RESPIRATORY FAILURE
alt_titles: MYOPATHY, PROXIMAL, WITH EARLY RESPIRATORY MUSCLE INVOLVEMENT
HEREDITARY MYOPATHY WITH EARLY RESPIRATORY FAILURE
MYOPATHY, DISTAL, WITH EARLY RESPIRATORY FAILURE, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT

relationships.phenotype: MYOPATHY, MYOFIBRILLAR, 9, WITH EARLY RESPIRATORY FAILURE

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that myofibrillar myopathy-9 with early respiratory failure (MFM9), also known as hereditary myopathy with early respiratory failure (HMERF), is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding titin (TTN; 188840) on chromosome 2q31.

checks.claim: Myofibrillar myopathy-9 with early respiratory failure (MFM9) is also known as hereditary myopathy with early respiratory failure (HMERF).
checks.evidence_quote: We suggest that HMERF due to mutations in the TTN gene be nosologically classified as MFM-titinopathy.
checks.explanation: Paper equates HMERF with MFM-titinopathy but does not use the designation MFM9.

checks.claim: MFM9/HMERF is caused by heterozygous mutation in the gene encoding titin (TTN).
checks.evidence_quote: Sequencing identified the heterozygous g.274375T>C mutation (p.C30071R) in 5/127 unrelated subjects
checks.explanation: Heterozygous TTN mutations cause HMERF/MFM-titinopathy.

checks.claim: The TTN gene is located on chromosome 2q31.
checks.evidence_quote: We recently mapped a locus for a new variant of autosomal dominant myopathy (Swedish families) with proximal muscle weakness, early respiratory muscle involvement, and unique muscle biopsy findings to chromosomal region 2q24-31.
checks.explanation: Standard gene location; the abstract places the Swedish HMERF locus at 2q24-31, consistent with 2q31. However, TTN is not named.

paragraphs.text: Myofibrillar myopathy-9 with early respiratory failure (MFM9), or hereditary myopathy with early respiratory failure (HMERF), is an autosomal dominant myopathy that usually begins in adulthood. Patients develop weakness that may be proximal or distal and involves the respiratory muscles early in the disease, so that respiratory failure may develop while the person can still walk. Muscle biopsies show myofibrillar changes with cytoplasmic bodies, eosinophilic inclusions, and rimmed vacuoles.

checks.claim: MFM9/HMERF is an autosomal dominant myopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Two Swedish families with autosomal dominant myopathy, who also had proximal weakness, early respiratory failure, and characteristic cytoplasmic bodies in the affected muscle biopsies
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the myopathy as autosomal dominant.

checks.claim: MFM9/HMERF usually begins in adulthood.
checks.evidence_quote: We describe a novel autosomal dominant myopathy presenting in mid-adult life with tibialis anterior weakness.
checks.explanation: Onset is in mid-adult life.

checks.claim: Patients with MFM9/HMERF develop weakness that may be proximal or distal.
checks.evidence_quote: The clinical presentation included predominant distal, proximal or respiratory muscle weakness.
checks.explanation: Weakness may be proximal or distal.

checks.claim: In MFM9/HMERF, the respiratory muscles are involved early in the disease.
checks.evidence_quote: Autosomal dominant myopathy with proximal weakness and early respiratory muscle involvement maps to chromosome 2q.
checks.explanation: The title states that the respiratory muscles are involved early.

checks.claim: In MFM9/HMERF, respiratory failure may develop while the patient is still ambulatory.
checks.evidence_quote: characterised by early respiratory failure whilst affected individuals were still ambulant
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies in MFM9/HMERF show myofibrillar changes with cytoplasmic bodies.
checks.evidence_quote: previous work on patients with the p.C30071R mutation has demonstrated Z-disc streaming, cytoplasmic bodies, and evidence of myofibrillar aggregation
checks.explanation: Myofibrillar changes and cytoplasmic bodies are described.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies in MFM9/HMERF show eosinophilic inclusions.
checks.evidence_quote: Fiber splitting, eosinophilic inclusions, and vacuoles with basophilic rims were seen in moderately affected muscles
checks.explanation: The abstract reports eosinophilic inclusions.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies in MFM9/HMERF show rimmed vacuoles.
checks.evidence_quote: Fiber splitting, eosinophilic inclusions, and vacuoles with basophilic rims were seen in moderately affected muscles
checks.explanation: Vacuoles with basophilic rims are rimmed vacuoles.

paragraphs.text: Edstrom et al. (1990) described a Swedish family with an autosomal dominant myopathy that began in adulthood. Affected members had proximal muscle weakness and early involvement of the respiratory muscles. Muscle biopsy showed cytoplasmic bodies and other myofibrillar abnormalities.

checks.claim: Edstrom et al. (1990) described a Swedish family with an autosomal dominant myopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: 16 patients representing 7 different pedigrees
checks.explanation: The paper describes 7 pedigrees, not a single family. Swedish origin is not stated, and autosomal dominant inheritance was evident only in a majority of cases.

checks.claim: The myopathy in the Swedish family described by Edstrom et al. (1990) began in adulthood.
checks.evidence_quote: 16 patients representing 7 different pedigrees exhibited an unusual, adult onset limb-girdle myopathy
checks.explanation: Adult onset is supported, but it applies to 7 pedigrees, not one Swedish family.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Swedish family described by Edstrom et al. (1990) had proximal muscle weakness.
checks.evidence_quote: adult onset limb-girdle myopathy
checks.explanation: A limb-girdle pattern means proximal weakness, but it was in 7 pedigrees, not a single Swedish family.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Swedish family described by Edstrom et al. (1990) had early involvement of the respiratory muscles.
checks.evidence_quote: A prominent early finding in all cases was respiratory muscle weakness
checks.explanation: Supported, but it applies to 7 pedigrees, not a single Swedish family.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsy in the Swedish family described by Edstrom et al. (1990) showed cytoplasmic bodies and other myofibrillar abnormalities.
checks.evidence_quote: Muscle biopsy findings revealed myofibrillar changes which, at the light microscopy level, included plaques that stained strongly with rhodamine-conjugated phalloidin
checks.explanation: Myofibrillar abnormalities (F-actin plaques and Z-disc changes) are reported, but cytoplasmic bodies are not mentioned in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: Chinnery et al. (2001) reported a British family with an autosomal dominant myopathy in which distal weakness was accompanied by early respiratory failure. Muscle pathology showed eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions and rimmed vacuoles. Linkage to known candidate loci was excluded.

checks.claim: Chinnery et al. (2001) reported a British family with an autosomal dominant myopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: We describe a novel autosomal dominant myopathy presenting in mid-adult life with tibialis anterior weakness. We carried out a detailed clinical assessment of 24 individuals spanning three generations
checks.explanation: The abstract confirms an autosomal dominant myopathy in one family but doesn't say the family is British.

checks.claim: In the British family reported by Chinnery et al. (2001), distal weakness was accompanied by early respiratory failure.
checks.evidence_quote: A novel autosomal dominant distal myopathy with early respiratory failure
checks.explanation: The title states both distal myopathy and early respiratory failure.

checks.claim: Muscle pathology in the British family reported by Chinnery et al. (2001) showed eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions.
checks.evidence_quote: Fiber splitting, eosinophilic inclusions, and vacuoles with basophilic rims were seen in moderately affected muscles
checks.explanation: The abstract reports eosinophilic inclusions. It doesn't use the word 'cytoplasmic', but this is a minor descriptive detail.

checks.claim: Muscle pathology in the British family reported by Chinnery et al. (2001) showed rimmed vacuoles.
checks.evidence_quote: Fiber splitting, eosinophilic inclusions, and vacuoles with basophilic rims were seen in moderately affected muscles
checks.explanation: Vacuoles with basophilic rims are rimmed vacuoles.

checks.claim: Chinnery et al. (2001) excluded linkage to known candidate loci in the British family.
checks.evidence_quote: The disease was not linked to any of the known loci associated with distal myopathies
checks.explanation: Linkage to the candidate loci was excluded. The family's nationality isn't stated in the abstract.

paragraphs.text: Pfeffer et al. (2012) and Ohlsson et al. (2012) reported further families from northern England and Sweden with HMERF. The degree of proximal versus distal weakness varied. Respiratory muscle weakness often appeared early, and many affected people needed noninvasive ventilation. Muscle MRI showed early involvement of the semitendinosus muscle. Biopsies showed cytoplasmic bodies, eosinophilic inclusions, and rimmed vacuoles. The heart was not usually affected.

checks.claim: Pfeffer et al. (2012) and Ohlsson et al. (2012) reported further families with HMERF from northern England and Sweden.
checks.evidence_quote: This segregated with the phenotype in 21 individuals from the original family, nine subjects in a second family
checks.explanation: Further families are reported, but the abstract does not say they came from northern England. Sweden relates to Ohlsson et al.

checks.claim: In the HMERF families reported by Pfeffer et al. (2012) and Ohlsson et al. (2012), the degree of proximal versus distal weakness varied.
checks.evidence_quote: The clinical presentation included predominant distal, proximal or respiratory muscle weakness.
checks.explanation: The predominant pattern of weakness varied between patients.

checks.claim: In the HMERF families reported by Pfeffer et al. (2012) and Ohlsson et al. (2012), respiratory muscle weakness often appeared early.
checks.evidence_quote: This disease should be considered in patients with adult-onset proximal or distal myopathy and early respiratory failure
checks.explanation: Respiratory involvement is described as early.

checks.claim: Many affected individuals in the HMERF families reported by Pfeffer et al. (2012) and Ohlsson et al. (2012) required noninvasive ventilation.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention noninvasive ventilation.

checks.claim: Muscle MRI in the HMERF families reported by Pfeffer et al. (2012) and Ohlsson et al. (2012) showed early involvement of the semitendinosus muscle.
checks.evidence_quote: revealed characteristic abnormalities with semitendinosus involvement in 20 of 21 patients studied, including 3 patients who were presymptomatic
checks.explanation: Semitendinosus involvement was present even in presymptomatic patients.

checks.claim: Muscle biopsies in the HMERF families reported by Pfeffer et al. (2012) and Ohlsson et al. (2012) showed cytoplasmic bodies, eosinophilic inclusions, and rimmed vacuoles.
checks.evidence_quote: Diagnostic muscle histopathology most frequently revealed eosinophilic inclusions (inclusion bodies) and rimmed vacuoles
checks.explanation: Eosinophilic inclusions and rimmed vacuoles are reported, but cytoplasmic bodies are not mentioned.

checks.claim: The heart was not usually affected in the HMERF families reported by Pfeffer et al. (2012) and Ohlsson et al. (2012).
checks.evidence_quote: Cardiomyopathy was not present in any of our patients despite up to 31 years of follow-up.
checks.explanation: No cardiomyopathy was found in any patient.

paragraphs.text: The families reported by Edstrom et al. (1990) and Chinnery et al. (2001) showed autosomal dominant inheritance.

checks.claim: The family reported by Edstrom et al. (1990) showed autosomal dominant inheritance of the myopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: In a majority of cases there was evidence of an autosomal dominant inheritance.
checks.explanation: Autosomal dominant inheritance was evident in a majority of cases across 7 pedigrees, not uniformly in one family.

checks.claim: The family reported by Chinnery et al. (2001) showed autosomal dominant inheritance of the myopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: We describe a novel autosomal dominant myopathy presenting in mid-adult life with tibialis anterior weakness.
checks.explanation: The family showed autosomal dominant inheritance across three generations.

paragraphs.text: Nicolao et al. (1999) studied a Swedish family with autosomal dominant myopathy, proximal weakness, and early respiratory muscle involvement. Using linkage analysis, they mapped the disorder to chromosome 2q24-q31.

checks.claim: Nicolao et al. (1999) studied a Swedish family with autosomal dominant myopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: Two Swedish families with autosomal dominant myopathy
checks.explanation: The paper studied two Swedish families, not one.

checks.claim: The Swedish family studied by Nicolao et al. (1999) had proximal weakness and early respiratory muscle involvement.
checks.evidence_quote: Two Swedish families with autosomal dominant myopathy, who also had proximal weakness, early respiratory failure
checks.explanation: The features are correct, but they were described in two families, not one.

checks.claim: Nicolao et al. (1999) mapped the myopathy in the Swedish family to chromosome 2q24-q31 by linkage analysis.
checks.evidence_quote: Linkage to the chromosomal region 2q24-q31 was established. A maximum combined two-point LOD score of 4.87
checks.explanation: Linkage to 2q24-q31 is correct, but it was established from the combined data of two families, not a single family.

paragraphs.text: Lange et al. (2005) studied the Swedish HMERF family and found a heterozygous arg279-to-trp (R279W) substitution in the kinase domain of TTN. They reported that this change altered binding of the kinase domain to its signaling partners. Later studies (Ohlsson et al., 2012; Pfeffer et al., 2012) found that this variant did not explain the disorder in the families studied. The causal mutation proved to lie in the A-band region of titin.

checks.claim: Lange et al. (2005) found a heterozygous arg279-to-trp (R279W) substitution in the kinase domain of TTN in the Swedish HMERF family.
checks.evidence_quote: A human mutation in the titin protein kinase domain causes hereditary muscle disease by disrupting this pathway.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a human mutation in the titin kinase domain. It does not specify R279W, heterozygosity, or a Swedish family; those details may be in the full text, which was not supplied.

checks.claim: Lange et al. (2005) reported that the TTN R279W substitution altered binding of the titin kinase domain to its signaling partners.
checks.evidence_quote: A human mutation in the titin protein kinase domain causes hereditary muscle disease by disrupting this pathway.
checks.explanation: The abstract says the mutation disrupts the TK–nbr1–p62–MuRF2 signaling pathway. It does not explicitly say that binding to signaling partners was altered, and it does not name R279W.

checks.claim: Later studies (Ohlsson et al., 2012; Pfeffer et al., 2012) found that the TTN R279W variant did not explain HMERF in the families studied.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention the R279W variant.

checks.claim: The causal HMERF mutation was found to lie in the A-band region of titin.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention the A-band region.

paragraphs.text: Ohlsson et al. (2012) studied Swedish families with HMERF. They identified a heterozygous cys30071-to-arg (C30071R) mutation in the A-band region of TTN, within fibronectin type III domain 119. The mutation segregated with the disorder in the families.

checks.claim: Ohlsson et al. (2012) studied Swedish families with HMERF.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 8 cited papers. This claim is about Ohlsson et al. (2012), which this paper does not address.

checks.claim: Ohlsson et al. (2012) identified a heterozygous cys30071-to-arg (C30071R) mutation in TTN in Swedish HMERF families.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 8 cited papers. The paper says Ohlsson's p.C30071R families are British: 'families A, B, C and F2 are from the Northumberland region'. It does not describe them as Swedish.

checks.claim: The TTN C30071R mutation lies in the A-band region of titin, within fibronectin type III domain 119.
checks.evidence_quote: p.C30071R in the 119th fibronectin-3 (FN3) domain
checks.explanation: The paper also says the mutations affect 'residues in the A-band of the protein'.

checks.claim: The TTN C30071R mutation segregated with HMERF in the Swedish families studied by Ohlsson et al. (2012).
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 8 cited papers. This paper reports no mutation segregation.

paragraphs.text: Pfeffer et al. (2012) studied British families with HMERF, including the family reported by Chinnery et al. (2001). They identified the same heterozygous C30071R mutation in TTN, which segregated with the disease. Haplotype analysis suggested a shared founder origin.

checks.claim: Pfeffer et al. (2012) studied British families with HMERF, including the family reported by Chinnery et al. (2001).
checks.evidence_quote: In 2001, we described an autosomal dominant myopathy characterized by neuromuscular ventilatory failure in ambulant patients.
checks.explanation: The original 2001 family plus additional families are studied, but the abstract does not say they were British.

checks.claim: Pfeffer et al. (2012) identified the heterozygous TTN C30071R mutation in British HMERF families.
checks.evidence_quote: the likely causal genetic variant in the titin (TTN) gene (g.274375T>C; p.Cys30071Arg)
checks.explanation: The C30071R variant is identified, but the abstract does not explicitly state heterozygosity or British origin.

checks.claim: The TTN C30071R mutation segregated with HMERF in the British families studied by Pfeffer et al. (2012).
checks.evidence_quote: This segregated with the phenotype in 21 individuals from the original family, nine subjects in a second family
checks.explanation: The variant segregated with the phenotype.

checks.claim: Haplotype analysis by Pfeffer et al. (2012) suggested a shared founder origin of the TTN C30071R mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: within a shared haplotype of 2.93 Mbp on chromosome 2
checks.explanation: A shared haplotype is consistent with a common founder origin.

paragraphs.text: Ohlsson et al. (2012) studied Swedish families with hereditary myopathy with early respiratory failure. They identified a heterozygous cys30071-to-arg (C30071R) mutation in fibronectin type III domain 119 of the A-band region of titin. The mutation segregated with the disorder.

checks.claim: Ohlsson et al. (2012) studied Swedish families with hereditary myopathy with early respiratory failure.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 8 cited papers. This claim is about Ohlsson et al. (2012), which this paper does not address.

checks.claim: Ohlsson et al. (2012) identified a heterozygous cys30071-to-arg (C30071R) mutation in titin in Swedish HMERF families.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 8 cited papers. The paper says Ohlsson's p.C30071R families are British: 'families A, B, C and F2 are from the Northumberland region'.

checks.claim: The titin C30071R mutation lies in fibronectin type III domain 119 of the A-band region of titin.
checks.evidence_quote: Recently, two novel titin (TTN) gene mutations, affecting residues in the A-band of the protein at p.C30071R and p.R32450W
checks.explanation: The abstract places p.C30071R in the 119th FN3 domain.

checks.claim: The titin C30071R mutation segregated with HMERF in the Swedish families studied by Ohlsson et al. (2012).
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 8 cited papers. This paper reports no mutation segregation.

paragraphs.text: Pfeffer et al. (2012) studied British families with HMERF and identified the same heterozygous C30071R mutation, which segregated with the disease.

checks.claim: Pfeffer et al. (2012) identified the heterozygous TTN C30071R mutation in British families with HMERF.
checks.evidence_quote: the likely causal genetic variant in the titin (TTN) gene (g.274375T>C; p.Cys30071Arg)
checks.explanation: The variant is identified, but British origin and heterozygosity are not explicitly stated in the abstract.

checks.claim: The TTN C30071R mutation segregated with HMERF in the British families studied by Pfeffer et al. (2012).
checks.evidence_quote: This segregated with the phenotype in 21 individuals from the original family, nine subjects in a second family
checks.explanation: The variant segregated with the disease.
